subject: SLA drift impact — exec brief & owners for QBR prep
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA drift on May 25 — initial postmortem notes

Team,

Quick summary of what we observed on May 25 between 02:10–03:45 UTC: a sudden task-queue backlog caused request queuing on the long-tail shard set (gpu-pool-us-west-2-b). That queue increased average P99 token latency by ~420ms for affected hosts and led to a partial SLO breach for the Dedicated tier (customer-visible window ~70 minutes).

Root cause (working hypothesis): a control-plane autoscale mis-evaluation triggered delayed eviction of stalled worker processes after a transient internal GC spike. The runtime continued accepting requests and KV cache pressure increased, exposing a path in the kernel selection logic that regressed latency for long sequences.

Impact snapshot attached (impact-snapshot.png) and CSV with SLO delta by customer (slo-delta-table.csv). Full draft postmortem lives here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cQBR-SLA-Postmortem (editable). I filed INF-4821 for the tracking epic.

Immediate mitigations applied (May 25):
- Emergency rollback of the kernel selection tweak to previous safe profile (Rishi/Runtime)
- Temporary throttle on Dedicated long-request routing to limit tail-load (Marcus/Serving)
- KV cache tuning to reduce memory pressure (Evelyn/Infra)

Ask for leadership brief: can we convert the draft into a one-page exec summary for the QBR (three bullets + three owners + crediting plan for affected customers)? I can draft but want guidance on tone and whether to propose a one-month SLA credit or a discretionary make-good for Atlas Retail.

Thanks,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@atlasretail.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA drift on May 25 — initial postmortem notes

Thanks for the quick triage, Rishi. Can you and Marcus produce a tight exec-facing brief by EOD Monday (Jun 31?) — sorry typo: by end of day Monday, May 31 — that contains:

1) One-line impact summary (customer-visible effect + duration)
2) Three root-cause bullets (concise)
3) Three mitigation/action items with owners and ETA (short, medium, long)

For the crediting ask: do not propose a blanket one-month credit yet. Prepare two options: a conservative service credit (30% of monthly bill for affected window) and an alternative discretionary credit (e.g., one-off invoice credit tied to specific customers). We'll decide after seeing Atlas Retail's impact slice.

Please flag anything that needs my exec sign-off in the body of the brief. Marcus — Evelyn — loop on numbers for the customer-slice. Vivek, FYI for QBR narrative; I want to mention the incident but frame it as an isolated regression corrected by kernel rollback and autoscale rule tuning.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference

Adding the numbers Sarah will want: per Atlas Retail the Dedicated instances saw a 12% drop in successful request throughput and a 2.8% increase in token-level error budget consumption during the window. Attached CSV (slo-delta-table.csv) has per-client rows.

Proposed short/medium/long actions (owners + ETA):
- Short (hours): Reinstate strict request admission control for long-seqs on Dedicated (owner: Marcus) — complete (May 25, hotfix).
- Medium (days): Add an autoscale safety net that forces worker eviction above a cache-pressure threshold (owner: Evelyn) — ETA: Jun 4.
- Long (weeks): Kernel selection overhaul with unit tests to block regressions for long sequences (owner: Rishi/Runtime) — ETA: Jul 15.

I also recommend we present a tidy 3-slide narrative for the QBR: 1) What happened + impact, 2) Root cause + mitigations, 3) Customer handling + credits/options. Kimberly — if you want, I can draft slide text.

—Marcus
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving

Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: SLA incident — exec brief (QBR-ready) + action register

Team & Sarah,

Attached is a condensed exec summary I drafted from the materials (postmortem-draft.md and the CSV). Below is the one-page brief for QBR and the action register for follow-up. Please treat this as the version I'll present unless you raise objections by EOD Wednesday.

Exec summary (one-paragraph + 3 bullets):
- One-paragraph: On May 25 a runtime kernel selection change combined with a transient autoscale mis-evaluation caused a tail latency regression affecting a subset of Dedicated hosts. The issue produced a ~70-minute customer-visible window for some customers (notably Atlas Retail) and marginally increased token-level error-budget consumption across affected tenants. The team performed an emergency rollback and admission-control hotfix to stop the tail latency; medium- and longer-term fixes are underway.

Three root-cause bullets:
1) Kernel selection regression exposed an untested long-seq codepath (Rishi)
2) Autoscale decision-making did not surface cache-pressure anomalies to the control plane (Evelyn)
3) Request admission controls lacked a hard threshold for Dedicated long-seq routing (Marcus)

Action register (owner — ETA — status):
- Rishi — implement kernel-selection unit tests & canary (ETA: 2027-07-15) — IN PROGRESS
- Evelyn — autoscale safety-net (cache-pressure eviction) (ETA: 2027-06-04) — PLANNED
- Marcus — formalize admission-control policy + regression tests (ETA: 2027-06-07) — COMPLETED (hotfix)
- Kimberly — customer crediting policy recommendation (ETA: 2027-06-03) — PENDING

Crediting options we will present at QBR:
A) Standard service credit: pro-rated percentage (example: 30% of monthly bill for impacted window) — straightforward accounting path
B) Discretionary invoice credit tied to specific remediation milestones — requires legal & procurement sign-off

Sarah — Procurement contact noted. If Atlas prefers option B, we will prepare a short form with accounting justification and an assigned contact (Evelyn will be primary accounting liaison for Credits).

Links & tracking: JIRA INF-4821, Postmortem doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cQBR-SLA-Postmortem. I will convert the above to two QBR slides and circulate draft by end of Wednesday.

Kimberly
VP, Customer Success & Operations
Redwood Inference
